events.title: Jin armies sack Kaifeng, capital of the Northern Song
events.description: In the Jingkang incident, Jurchen troops of the Jin dynasty sacked Kaifeng and carried off the Song emperors Qinzong and Huizong. The Song court fled south, where it ruled as the Southern Song.
events.html: In the Jingkang incident, Jurchen troops of the Jin dynasty sacked Kaifeng and carried off the Song emperors Qinzong and Huizong. The Song court fled south, where it ruled as the Southern Song.

events.title: Trial of Joan of Arc opens in Rouen
events.description: A church court led by Bishop Pierre Cauchon, an ally of the English, began proceedings against Joan of Arc on charges of heresy. She was condemned and burned at the stake on 30 May.
events.html: A church court led by Bishop Pierre Cauchon, an ally of the English, began proceedings against Joan of Arc on charges of heresy. She was condemned and burned at the stake on 30 May.

events.title: First shock of the great Sicilian earthquake strikes
events.description: A strong foreshock damaged towns across south-eastern Sicily. Two days later the main earthquake devastated the region, killing some 60,000 people and leading to the Baroque rebuilding of Noto and Catania.
events.html: A strong foreshock damaged towns across south-eastern Sicily. Two days later the main earthquake devastated the region, killing some 60,000 people and leading to the Baroque rebuilding of Noto and Catania.

events.title: Connecticut ratifies the US Constitution
events.description: Connecticut's convention approved the Constitution by 128 votes to 40, making it the fifth state to ratify. Nine states were needed for the new frame of government to take effect.
events.html: Connecticut's convention approved the Constitution by 128 votes to 40, making it the fifth state to ratify. Nine states were needed for the new frame of government to take effect.

events.title: Treaty of Jassy ends the Russo-Turkish War
events.description: The Ottoman Empire recognised Russia's annexation of Crimea and ceded the coast between the Bug and Dniester rivers. The treaty confirmed Russia as the dominant power on the northern Black Sea.
events.html: The Ottoman Empire recognised Russia's annexation of Crimea and ceded the coast between the Bug and Dniester rivers. The treaty confirmed Russia as the dominant power on the northern Black Sea.

events.title: Blanchard makes the first balloon flight in North America
events.description: Watched by President George Washington, the French aeronaut Jean-Pierre Blanchard ascended from a prison yard in Philadelphia. He landed some 46 minutes later in Deptford, New Jersey.
events.html: Watched by President George Washington, the French aeronaut Jean-Pierre Blanchard ascended from a prison yard in Philadelphia. He landed some 46 minutes later in Deptford, New Jersey.

events.title: Pitt's income tax becomes law in Britain
events.description: William Pitt the Younger's income tax, set at two shillings in the pound on higher incomes, received royal assent to fund the war against Revolutionary France. Abolished in 1816, it returned for good in 1842.
events.html: William Pitt the Younger's income tax, set at two shillings in the pound on higher incomes, received royal assent to fund the war against Revolutionary France. Abolished in 1816, it returned for good in 1842.

events.title: Admiral Nelson is buried in St Paul's Cathedral
events.description: After a vast procession through London, Horatio Nelson was laid to rest in the crypt of St Paul's. He had been killed at his victory at Trafalgar the previous October.
events.html: After a vast procession through London, Horatio Nelson was laid to rest in the crypt of St Paul's. He had been killed at his victory at Trafalgar the previous October.

events.title: Cadets fire on the Star of the West in Charleston Harbor
events.description: Southern guns fired on the merchant ship Star of the West as it tried to resupply Fort Sumter, forcing it to turn back. The shots are sometimes called the first of the American Civil War.
events.html: Southern guns fired on the merchant ship Star of the West as it tried to resupply Fort Sumter, forcing it to turn back. The shots are sometimes called the first of the American Civil War.

events.title: Last Allied troops evacuate Gallipoli
events.description: British troops left Cape Helles, ending the Gallipoli campaign in an Ottoman victory. The evacuation was the most successful part of an eight-month operation that cost well over 100,000 lives on both sides.
events.html: British troops left Cape Helles, ending the Gallipoli campaign in an Ottoman victory. The evacuation was the most successful part of an eight-month operation that cost well over 100,000 lives on both sides.

events.title: Juan de la Cierva's autogiro makes its first successful flight
events.description: At Getafe near Madrid, the Spanish engineer's C.4 autogiro flew using a freely turning rotor for lift. The design pioneered rotor technology later used in helicopters.
events.html: At Getafe near Madrid, the Spanish engineer's C.4 autogiro flew using a freely turning rotor for lift. The design pioneered rotor technology later used in helicopters.

events.title: Anthony Eden resigns as British Prime Minister
events.description: Citing ill health, Eden stepped down two months after the Suez Crisis, in which Britain and France had been forced by American pressure to withdraw from Egypt. Harold Macmillan succeeded him.
events.html: Citing ill health, Eden stepped down two months after the Suez Crisis, in which Britain and France had been forced by American pressure to withdraw from Egypt. Harold Macmillan succeeded him.
